electroweak_higgs.identity: electroweak radial mode = observed 125 GeV Higgs (F73)
electroweak_higgs.note: observed at LHC; decays to bb/WW/ZZ -> not dark matter

Eg_amplitude_mode.identity: E_g second-shell condensate amplitude mode (sets lepton masses, F93 O1)

angular_mode.note: even if long-lived (if below e+e- threshold), it is far too rare to be the DM (F198)

freezeout_moot.conclusion: freeze-out abundance is undefined for an unstable state; the WIMP window of F198 cannot be realised by the E_g amplitude mode

viable_relic_requirement.requirement: a conserved charge (Z2/U(1)) making the relic the LIGHTEST state carrying it, so it cannot decay to SM
viable_relic_requirement.why_not: the E_g amplitude mode is even under the D_2h stabilizer and couples linearly to the lepton mass operator (its defining role) -> no symmetry forbids S -> l+l-
model_native_candidates: a STERILE-sector excitation (no SM gauge charge; F191 'sterile-sector' hint)
a topologically conserved lattice excitation (orthorhombic-domain texture / skyrmion of U(x)) carrying a winding number
the lightest state of a hidden conserved lattice charge (a 'dark baryon', Z3-centre analog of F97)

verdict: Working out the amplitude mode from F73/F93: the EW radial mode is the observed 125 GeV Higgs (decays), and the E_g second-shell amplitude mode couples to leptons as g_l=m_l/f (it IS the lepton-mass crystal field), so it decays in ~1e-21 s — 38 orders below cosmological. Omega_DM=0.26 does NOT fall out: the E_g sector has no STABLE relic. The obstruction moves from abundance to stability/identity — dark matter needs a conserved charge the E_g condensate lacks (sterile sector / topological winding / hidden conserved charge).
